current_evidence: Cumberland's 'Apply for planning permission' page still sends applicants to separate legacy area pages for Allerdale, Carlisle and Copeland, plus a Cumbria minerals and waste page. The Allerdale page links the Allerdale full validation checklist and its type-specific checklists (2025-03 uploads, no dates in the page text). A single Cumberland-wide checklist went out to consultation (comments by 9 May 2025, publication planned May 2025), but none was found published. The URL given here covers only the Allerdale area.

issues.detail: Grokbot's PDF is the former Cumbria County Council list 'Local planning validation requirements for Minerals, Waste and County Council planning applications', dated November 2021. It covers county matters only, not Cumberland's general local validation requirements. Those are still the legacy Allerdale, Carlisle and Copeland area checklists on the 'Apply for planning permission' area pages.
issues.evidence: Cover: 'Cumbria County Council' / 'Local planning validation requirements for Minerals, Waste and County Council planning applications' / 'November 2021'; Part 2 checklists: Minerals Development, Waste Development, County Council Developments

issues.detail: The list date 2014-03-01 ('published in March 2014') is wrong. That phrase describes the National Planning Practice Guidance, not this list. The document's cover date is November 2021. It still counts as outdated (more than 2 years old), but for a different reason.
issues.evidence: Section 1.1: NPPG is a web-based resource 'first published in March 2014 and regularly updated'; cover line 'November 2021'

issues.detail: Grokbot put every requirement under 'Full planning' (INFERRED) and marked 'Minerals & waste (county)' as '(none) - national requirements only'. In fact the whole document applies only to minerals, waste and Regulation 3 county council applications, so the rows are inverted. Examples: Noise, Dust, LVIA, Minerals restoration and Planning Obligations should all sit under Minerals & waste / Reg 3, not Full planning.
issues.evidence: Document title and Part 2 checklists 'Minerals Development', 'Waste Development', 'County Council Developments'

issues.detail: Grokbot missed nine requirements in the document it read. (1) Air Quality Assessment: emissions to air (dust, odour, stack, traffic), or sites in or next to an AQMA. (2) Birdstrike Assessment: open quarrying, landfill, sewage or outfall works, or features that attract birds, within 13km of Carlisle or Walney Island airfields. (3) Blasting Scheme: blasting with explosives for minerals development. (4) Cumulative Impact Assessment: where impacts could worsen in combination with other developments. (5) Minerals Need Assessment: all minerals extraction proposals. (6) Public Rights of Way Statement: proposals that may affect a public right of way. (7) Site Waste Management Plan: site excavation or building demolition. (8) Utilities Assessment: major schemes. Grokbot's 'Foul Sewage / Utilities Statement' row is foul drainage text. (9) Biodiversity & Geodiversity: geology and quarry works triggers that the ecology row does not capture.
issues.evidence: Section 4 local requirements headings: Air Quality Assessment, Birdstrike Assessment, Blasting Scheme, Cumulative Impact Assessment, Minerals Need Assessment, Public Rights of Way Statement, Site Waste Management Plan, Utilities Assessment

issues.detail: Grokbot shows Householder, Outline, Listed building consent and other types as 'No specific local requirements - national only', but the legacy area lists in force do set local requirements. For example, the Allerdale area publishes separate checklists for householder, replacement windows and doors, householder larger rear extension prior approval, listed building, change of use, agricultural and equestrian buildings, wind turbines, and minor and major full and outline applications. They come with appendices on windows and doors, heritage, a countryside building conversion contamination form, ecology, tree survey, FRA, the NW SuDS pro-forma and a foul drainage form. Housing in identified river catchments must also show nutrient neutrality. None of these were captured.
issues.evidence: cumberland.gov.uk/planning-and-building-control/apply-planning-permission-allerdale: 'there are new validation requirements' ... housing in identified river catchments must 'demonstrate nutrient neutrality'

issues.detail: Most excerpts are 'When required' headings with page numbers or references attached, not the actual triggers. Tree Survey: 'assessment required Tree Surveys When required 33'. Coal Mining: 'Regulations 1999 Coal Mining Risk Assessment When required' (the actual trigger is development in Coal Authority high-risk areas). Land contamination: 'and Toolkit Land Contamination Survey / Risk Assessment When required' (actual: likely contamination, or within about 250m of landfill). Economic Statement: '023-032 (27-201403060) Economic Statement When required' (actual: major proposals with significant employment impact). Statement of Community Involvement: 'highway authority Statement of Community Involvement When required' (actual: major proposals and those with an ES). Drainage: 'well-designed places) Drainage Details... When required' (actual: all development). The Noise, Heritage, Ventilation and Planning Obligations rows follow the same pattern, as do 'its proposed restoration scheme' (Minerals) and 'levels of sunlight to be determined.' (Daylight).
issues.evidence: Grokbot trigger_excerpt fields vs source 'When required' paragraphs in section 4

issues.detail: The 'County own devt (Reg 3)' row is labelled 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details', but its text is process guidance about ticking 'is for Waste Management' or 'comes under Regulation 3' when applying online, and says the council will not validate incomplete applications. It is not a refuse storage requirement.
issues.evidence: Grokbot excerpt: '"is for Waste Management" or "comes under Regulation 3" ... at Step 2 of "starting an online application". 2.9 The council will not register or validate an application if it is incomplete'

issues.detail: Several items are boilerplate or national requirements, not local ones. The 'Submission rules' tab item is checklist-usage and validation-dispute text that ends mid-heading ('4 PART 1 2.0 PRE-APPLICATION AND VALIDATI'). One 'Policy-driven requirements' item is just a definition list of designated sites. The 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' row is a fragment of the LVIA guidance. 'Design and Access Statement' and 'Block plan / Site plan' come from section 3.0 (national requirements), not the local list.
issues.evidence: Section 3.0 National validation requirements vs section 4.0 Local validation requirements

issues.detail: The 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' and 'Habitats Regulations Assessment' rows share one sentence about the 'likelihood of EIA/HRA being a requirement', which states neither trigger. The EIA trigger is Schedule 1 and some Schedule 2 development; HRA applies where a European site may be affected. 'Photographs / Photomontages' is part of the LVIA requirement, not a separate one.
issues.evidence: Both rows: 'likelihood of EIA/HRA being a requirement for their application, so they can take the timetable and need for specialist ecology input into account...'

issues.detail: Grokbot did not record that Cumberland consulted on a new single Local Validation Checklist, in three parts: national requirements, a Local List, and a minerals and waste Local List. Comments closed on 9 May 2025 and publication was planned for May 2025, but no adopted Cumberland-wide list was found on the planning pages. The PDF probably came from planning.data.gov.uk, which registers it as Cumberland's 'Local Planning Validation Requirements' (start date 2024-01-01, entry date 2026-10-16) even though it is the county-matters list.
issues.claude_response: Grok could not verify this, so the finding stands until someone checks it by hand.

summary: Grokbot's link opens, but it is the inherited Cumbria County Council minerals, waste and Reg 3 list (November 2021, not March 2014), and its rows sit under Full planning when they belong under Minerals & waste. Cumberland's general requirements are still the legacy Allerdale, Carlisle and Copeland area checklists, none of which were captured. Even within the M&W list, nine requirements (e.g. Birdstrike, Blasting, Minerals Need, PRoW) are missing and most triggers are fragments.
